claims.event: Born in the twelfth month of Wanli 38. Personal name Youjian; fifth son of Guangzong. The annals title him Zhuanglie, with the death epithet Min.
Enfeoffed Prince of Xin in Tianqi 2.
In the eleventh month of Tianqi 6 he moved out to the Prince of Xin's residence.

In the eighth month of the next year, Tianqi 7, he was summoned as Xizong's illness became critical, received the testament, and on dingsi took the throne. He proclaimed an amnesty and named the next year Chongzhen 1.
In the ninth month he posthumously titled his birth mother Empress Xiaochun, suspended executions, and invested Consort Zhou as empress.
In the tenth month, on the new moon jiawu, he sacrificed at the Grand Temple.

In the eleventh month Wei Zhongxian was sent to confinement at Fengyang. Frontier eunuch overseers were recalled. Restitution on officials put to death under Tianqi was remitted and their families freed.

Chongzhen 1. Eunuchs were barred from the gates without orders. Ministers were warned not to cultivate eunuchs. He attended the Classics Lectern, buried Xizong at Deling, honored officials unjustly condemned, gave the jinshi degrees, appointed Yuan Chonghuan, refused Zhuo Ming's mines, ordered the Records of Three Reigns Essentials destroyed, abolished supernumerary posts, prayed for rain, and restored long tenure and joint liability for recommendations. He struck Feng Quan and Wei Guangwei from the registers, held an audience at the Ping Platform, met his ministers daily at the Wenhua Hall except in extreme weather, sacrificed to Heaven at the Southern Suburb, and ended stipends to the tribes beyond Guangning and Ji. Those tribes' request to buy grain was refused.

Chongzhen 2. Offered the libation to Confucius, sacrificed at the altars of soil and grain and to Earth, proclaimed amnesty at Cilang's birth, fasted in the Wenhua Hall during drought, and ordered ministers to the defense. The annal records Zhao Shuaijiao's death on yiyou before Zunhua's fall on jiashen, and the wuzi relief columns after Yuan's xinmao encampment, although those day-pairs run backward in the cycle.

Chongzhen 3. Installed Cilang as heir and proclaimed amnesty, fasted again in drought, forbade copying frontier reports, suspended executions, raised the land tax for supplies, and received tribute from U-Tsang.

Nanjing vice minister of rites. On gengxu he was made minister of rites and grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: Died on wuchen in the tenth month.
Vice minister of rites. On guisi he and He Wuzou were made ministers of rites and grand secretaries.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: Vice minister of rites. Made a grand secretary with Wang Yingxiong. The English writes He Wuyao; the name is 何吾騶.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: Deputy general on Guanglu Island. On jichou he surrendered to the Great Qing.

Yansui grand coordinator, made vice minister of war and governor-general of Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Huguang. In the sixth month he joined Lu Xiangsheng at Shangjin. In the summer he accepted the feigned surrender at Chexiang Gorge and let the rebels out; they rebelled again. On gengchen in the eleventh month he was imprisoned and sentenced to exile. The text does not say he had yet gone into exile.
Routed bandits at Lingbao. On yisi he was defeated at Wulingshan. After the gorge surrender he pursued from Qingshui and was defeated again.
On jiashen he plowed the sacred field. The court later ordered the combined campaign and the frontier defense.
On yiyou he broke into Shangzhou and Luozhou. Thirteen camps streamed into southern Han.
On jiachen he and unnamed others received the jinshi in graded ranks. The English writes Liu Shun; the name is 劉理順.
Vice general. On gengxu he pursued bandits from Sichuan into Huguang and routed them at Shihekou.

Vice general. On bingshen he and others defeated bandits at Lantian. On renyin in the intercalary month Li Zicheng besieged him at Longzhou. Hong Chengchou later raised the siege. The others at Lantian are not named.
Censor-in-chief directing pacification at Yunyang. On xinwei he joined Chen Qiyu at Shangjin against the Huguang bandits.
With Li Zicheng and their followers, besieged two months in Chexiang Gorge. They feigned surrender, were released, and rebelled again. The followers are not named.

Besieged with Gao Yingxiang, then rebelled again. On renyin he besieged He Renlong at Longzhou. That winter he took Chenzhou. The annal dates Hong Chengchou's relief on gengchen and the combined-campaign edict on jiaxu, though jiaxu precedes gengchen in the cycle.
On yiwei he was ordered to hold Juyong.
Baoding grand coordinator. Ordered, with others not named, to hold Zijing and Yanmen. The English writes Ding Kuitai; the name is 丁魁楚.
In the eighth month he and other regional commanders, not named, were sent to reinforce the frontier.
Vice minister and Xuanda governor-general. On wuchen he commanded the relief armies of the garrisons.
In the intercalary month bandits took Longde and Guyuan. He marched to relieve them and was killed.
On gengchen he lifted the siege of Longzhou. On yiyou he was also given military affairs of the five provinces.

label.en: Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Five Provinces

claims.event: Vice general with the Huguang relief of Hanzhong. Killed in battle on gengxu.
Marched out against the bandits, concentrated at Ruzhou, returned to Lingbao, directed Cao Bianjiao's victory at Guanshan, and defeated Lao Huihui at Lintong.

Took Yingzhou, Fengyang, Lujiang and Wuwei, then Qianshan, Luotian, Taihu, and Xincai until Zhang Guowei drove him back. He raided Pingliang and Fengxiang, broke through Zhuyang Pass, and later joined Li Zicheng.
Garrison commander at Fengyang. Died fighting when the city fell and the tomb halls burned. Others who died with him are not named.

Fled to Guide and re-entered Shaanxi with Luo Rucai. Ai Wannian and Liu Guozhen were killed attacking him. He took Xianyang; Gao Jie surrendered. He fled east, joined Zhang Xianzhong, took Shanzhou, and was defeated at Queshan.
With Li Zicheng he re-entered Shaanxi.
Yingtian grand coordinator. Drove Zhang Xianzhong back.
Minister and grain-transport grand coordinator. Arrested because the imperial tombs were lost, and soon executed in the market.
Defeated bandits at Luoshan. On yisi Sichuan troops mutinied at Fancheng and he killed himself.
Defeated bandits at Suizhou. On bingwu he pursued them to Qiutou Fort, fell into an ambush, and died fighting. The English writes Cao Wenchao; the name is 曹文詔.
On dinghai he defeated Liu Xiang. Xiang's followers, not named, all surrendered.
Pirate. After Zheng Zhilong defeated him he killed himself.
On yihai in the fifth month he retired.
Vice general. On renchen he and Liu Guozhen attacked Li Zicheng at Xiangle in Ningzhou and were killed.
Vice general. Killed with Ai Wannian.
Junior mentor. On jiaxu he and Zhang Zhifa were made vice ministers of rites and grand secretaries. On gengxu in the eleventh month he was dismissed with He Wuzou.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: Vice minister of punishments. Made vice minister of rites and grand secretary.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: Regional commander. Defeated when Zhang Xianzhong broke through Zhuyang Pass. The bandits fled into Henan.
Bandit general. Surrendered when Li Zicheng took Xianyang.
On xinchou he was made supreme commander for Zhili, Henan, Shandong, Huguang, and Sichuan. On yiyou he and Zu Kuan defeated Li Zicheng at Queshan.
Vice general. Under Hong Chengchou he and others defeated bandits at Guanshan Fort. The others are not named.
Regional commander. Captured when the army was defeated at Wadian in Shenqiu.
On renshen he retired.

Withdrew eunuch supervisors except at the capital and the Shanhai and Ning fronts. On gengchen he issued a self-reproach edict, moved to the Wuying Hall, and cut meals and music. He approved Hou Xun's tax demand and sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb.
Minister of revenue. Asked for strict collection of overdue taxes. Approved.
On gengxu he and Wen Zhenmeng were dismissed. The English writes He Wuyao; the name is 何吾騶.
Defeated bandits at Ruzhou, then with Lu Xiangsheng defeated Li Zicheng at Queshan.
On wuzi he defeated bandits at Wenxiang.
Led bandits from Henan into Shaanxi. Hong Chengchou defeated them at Lintong. The name is the sobriquet Lao Huihui.

On jiayin he and Zu Kuan relieved Chuzhou and routed the bandits at Zhulong Bridge. In the third month he and Zu Dale campaigned in Henan. On yiwei in the eighth month he encamped at Zhending on the way to the capital. The English dates that day yimao; the text says 乙未. On xinyou he was made governor-general of Xuan-Da and Shanxi.
With Lu Xiangsheng he routed the bandits at Zhulong Bridge while relieving Chuzhou.
On dingmao he was restored to vice minister of rites and made a grand secretary. On yihai in the sixth month he died.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: Former vice general. Fought the bandits at Songxian and was killed.
Ningxia grand coordinator. Mutinous troops killed him during the famine.
Military vice commissioner. Pacified the Ningxia mutiny after Wang Ji was killed.
Military licentiate. On xinmao he was made a supervising secretary.
With Lu Xiangsheng he campaigned against the Henan bandits. The text does not state a kinship with Zu Kuan.
With Li Zicheng he entered Shaanxi. On renxu Sun Chuanting captured him at Zhouzhi. He was sent to the capital and executed.
Entered Shaanxi with Gao Yingxiang. Yu Chongxiao was killed attacking him at Anding. He raided Yulin and He Renlong routed him.
On wuzi in the fourth month he retired.
Yan-Sui regional commander. On bingchen he attacked Li Zicheng at Anding, was defeated, and was killed.
Routed Li Zicheng when he raided Yulin.
Vice minister of personnel. On jiashen he, He Fengsheng, and Huang Shijun were made ministers of rites and grand secretaries. The English calls the pavilion the Eastern Lodge; the text says 東閣.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: Minister of rites. Made a grand secretary with Kong Zhenyun and Huang Shijun.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: Minister of rites. Made a grand secretary with the other two.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: On jihai, while pacifying bandits at Xichuan, he was killed.
Eunuch. On jiachen he and others were assigned to hold Zijing, Daoma, and other passes. The others are not named.
Duke of Chengguo. On gengxu he inspected the frontier passes.
Censor inspecting the passes. Killed when Qing forces entered Changping. Others who died are not named.
Shaanxi grand coordinator. On renxu he captured Gao Yingxiang at Zhouzhi and sent him to the capital for execution.
Minister of war. On jiazi he commanded the relief army, with Gao Qiqian as grand overseer.
Made grand overseer of the relief army under Zhang Fengyi. This unit does not call him a eunuch.
Prince of Tang. On bingshen he raised troops to aid the throne, was forced back to his fief, and was soon reduced to a commoner.
Vice minister of works. On yihai he was struck from the registers for memorializing against the eunuchs and Grand Secretary Wen Tiren.
Grand secretary. Liu Zongzhou's memorial against him and the eunuchs led to Liu's dismissal, not to a recorded penalty for Wen.
On jiashen he raided Xiangyang.
Defeated the bandits at Longzhou. They fled toward Qingyang and Fengxiang.
On bingwu his bands moved north of the Yangzi. The English calls them Muslim rebel bands; the text names 老回回.
With Luo Rucai he marched from Xiangyang against Anqing. Nanjing was alarmed.
With Zhang Xianzhong he attacked Anqing.
On dingyou he and Shi Kefa defeated bandits at Maple-fragrance Post (楓香驛). The English says Fengxiang Post. On bingzi in the ninth month he defeated bandits at Hong County.
Vice commissioner. With Zuo Liangyu he defeated the Qianshan raiders.
On dingsi he and unnamed others received the jinshi in graded ranks.
Vice regional commander. Died fighting when Qing forces took Pi Island.
Regional commander. Fled from Pi Island to Shicheng Island.
Suppressed bandits in southern Han, defeated them at Hanzhong, and with Cao Bianjiao encamped at Guangyuan to relieve Sichuan.

Governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi and censor-in-chief. Made minister of war and supreme commander of Nanjing, Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Huguang, stationed at Yunyang. The English writes Shandong for 山.

On wuyin he marched from Qinzhou into Sichuan. On guisi he took Ningqiang. On bingshen he entered western Sichuan by Qipan Pass, took Zhaohua, Jianzhou, and Zitong, and pressed Chengdu. Hou Liangzhu was killed.
On wushen in the sixth month he retired.
Vice minister of personnel. On jiyou he was made minister of rites and a grand secretary. The English says Eastern Lodge; the text says 東閣.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: Vice minister of rites. Made minister of rites and a grand secretary.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: Vice censor-in-chief. Made vice minister of rites and a grand secretary.

label.en: Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion

claims.event: On guimao in the twelfth month he retired.
Regional commander. Killed as Li Zicheng took the Sichuan counties and pressed Chengdu.
On guihai he and Hong Chengchou encamped at Guangyuan to relieve Sichuan.

translationRepairs: In the third month, on jisi, Emperor Xizong was buried at Deling.
In the third month, on jisi, Emperor Zhe (Xizong) was buried at Deling.
悊皇帝 is the posthumous title Zhe, not the temple name Xizong.
Third month, day jisi: the Ti Emperor was buried at Deling.
Third month, day jisi: Emperor Zhe (Xizong) was buried at Deling.
悊 is Zhe, not Ti. It is Xizong's posthumous title.
In the fifth month, on jisi, Li Guozhen retired from office.
In the fifth month, on jisi, Li Guopu retired from office.
李國𣚴 is the taboo form of 普 (Guopu), not Guozhen.
Fifth month, day jisi: Li Guozhen retired from office.
Fifth month, day jisi: Li Guopu retired from office.
李國𣚴 is the taboo form of 普 (Guopu), not Guozhen.
On jiashen the Ningyuan garrison mutinied, and grand coordinator Bi Zisheng took his own life.
On jiashen the Ningyuan garrison mutinied, and grand coordinator Bi Zisu took his own life.
肅 is su. 畢自肅 is Bi Zisu, not Bi Zisheng.
Day jiashen: the Ningyuan garrison mutinied; Grand Coordinator Bi Zisheng killed himself.
Day jiashen: the Ningyuan garrison mutinied; Grand Coordinator Bi Zisu killed himself.
肅 is su. 畢自肅 is Bi Zisu, not Bi Zisheng.
On jiashen Great Qing forces took Zunhua; grand coordinator Wang Yuanya, assistant magistrate He Tianqiu, and others were killed.
On jiashen Great Qing forces took Zunhua; grand coordinator Wang Yuanya, prefectural judge (tuiguan) He Tianqiu, and others were killed.
推官 is a prefectural judge, not a county assistant magistrate.
Day jiashen: Great Qing forces entered Zunhua; Grand Coordinator Wang Yuanya, Assistant Magistrate He Tianqiu, and others died.
Day jiashen: Great Qing forces entered Zunhua; Grand Coordinator Wang Yuanya, Prefectural Judge (tuiguan) He Tianqiu, and others died.
推官 is a prefectural judge, not a county assistant magistrate.
In the fifth month, on xinmao, the armies of Ma Shilong, Zu Dashou, and others entered Luzhou.
In the fifth month, on xinmao, the armies of Ma Shilong, Zu Dashou, and others entered Luanzhou.
灤州 is Luanzhou, the same prefecture named Luanzhou when it fell, not Luzhou.
Fifth month, day xinmao: the armies of Ma Shilong, Zu Dashou, and others entered Luzhou.
Fifth month, day xinmao: the armies of Ma Shilong, Zu Dashou, and others entered Luanzhou.
灤州 is Luanzhou, the same prefecture named Luanzhou when it fell, not Luzhou.
On guiwei Yang He, commissioner for the Three Frontiers in Shaanxi, induced roving rebels to submit at Ningzhou; the bands feigned surrender and soon rose again.
On guiwei Yang He, vice minister and governor-general of the Three Frontiers of Shaanxi, induced roving rebels to submit at Ningzhou; the bands feigned surrender and soon rose again.
侍郎 is vice minister, and 總督 is governor-general, not a generic commissioner.
That month Yansui Vice General Cao Wenbiao attacked rebels at Hequ, and Wang Jiayin was defeated and killed.
That month Yansui Vice General Cao Wenzhao attacked rebels at Hequ, and Wang Jiayin was defeated and killed.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
That month Yansui Vice General Cao Wenbiao attacked rebels at Hequ, and Wang Jiayin was defeated and killed.
That month Yansui Vice General Cao Wenzhao attacked rebels at Hequ, and Wang Jiayin was defeated and killed.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
In the seventh month of autumn, on jiaxu, Regional Commander Wang Jien defeated rebels at Fuzhou and received the surrender of the rebel chieftain Shang Tianlong.
In the seventh month of autumn, on jiaxu, Regional Commander Wang Ji'en defeated rebels at Fu Prefecture (鄜州) and received the surrender of the rebel chieftain Shang Tianlong.
際恩 is Ji'en, not Jien. 鄜州 is Fu Prefecture in Shaanxi, not Fuzhou.
Autumn, seventh month, day jiaxu: Regional Commander Wang Jien defeated rebels at Fuzhou and received the surrender of the rebel chieftain Shang Tianlong.
Autumn, seventh month, day jiaxu: Regional Commander Wang Ji'en defeated rebels at Fu Prefecture (鄜州) and received the surrender of the rebel chieftain Shang Tianlong.
際恩 is Ji'en, not Jien. 鄜州 is Fu Prefecture in Shaanxi, not Fuzhou.
In the eighth month, on maoyin, Regional Commander He Huchen attacked and beheaded the rebel Liu Liu at Qingyang.
In the eighth month, on guimao, Regional Commander He Huchen attacked and beheaded the rebel Liu Liu at Qingyang.
癸卯 is guimao, not maoyin.
Eighth month, day maoyin: Regional Commander He Huchen attacked and beheaded the rebel Liu Liu at Qingyang.
Eighth month, day guimao: Regional Commander He Huchen attacked and beheaded the rebel Liu Liu at Qingyang.
癸卯 is guimao, not maoyin.

On wuxu Shanhai Regional Commander Song Wei and others marched to relieve Daling, were defeated at Changshan, and Zhang Chun, supervising secretary of the Court of Imperial Studs who oversaw the army, was taken captive.

On wuxu Shanhai Regional Commander Song Wei and others marched to relieve Daling, were defeated at Changshan, and Zhang Chun, vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and army supervisor, was taken captive.
太僕少卿 is vice minister of the Imperial Stud. 監軍 is army supervisor, not a supervising secretary (給事中).

Day wuxu: Shanhai Regional Commander Song Wei and others went to relieve Daling, were defeated at Changshan, and Supervising Secretary of the Court of Imperial Studs Zhang Chun, who oversaw the army, was taken captive.

Day wuxu: Shanhai Regional Commander Song Wei and others went to relieve Daling, were defeated at Changshan, and Zhang Chun, Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and army supervisor, was taken captive.
太僕少卿 is vice minister of the Imperial Stud. 監軍 is army supervisor, not a supervising secretary.
In spring of Chongzhen five, on xinchou of the first month, Kong Youde captured Dengzhou; Guerrilla Commander Chen Liangmo died fighting, and Regional Commander Zhang Kedai died in the affair.
In spring of Chongzhen five, on xinchou of the first month, Kong Youde captured Dengzhou; Guerrilla Commander Chen Liangmo died fighting, and Regional Commander Zhang Keda died in the affair.
可大 is Keda. 張可大 is Zhang Keda, not Zhang Kedai.
Year five, spring, first month, day xinchou: Kong Youde took Dengzhou; Guerrilla Commander Chen Liangmo died fighting, and Regional Commander Zhang Kedai died in the affair.
Year five, spring, first month, day xinchou: Kong Youde took Dengzhou; Guerrilla Commander Chen Liangmo died fighting, and Regional Commander Zhang Keda died in the affair.
可大 is Keda. 張可大 is Zhang Keda, not Zhang Kedai.

That month Regional Commanders Cao Wenbiao and Yang Jiamou repeatedly defeated rebels at Long'an and Jingning; the rebels fled to Shuiluo Fort, famine victims of Pingliang and Zhuanglang rallied to them, and their power revived.

That month Regional Commanders Cao Wenzhao and Yang Jiamou repeatedly defeated rebels at Long'an and Jingning; the rebels fled to Shuiluo Fort, famine victims of Pingliang and Zhuanglang rallied to them, and their power revived.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.

That month Regional Commanders Cao Wenbiao and Yang Jiamou repeatedly defeated rebels at Long'an and Jingning; the rebels fled to Shuiluo Fort, and famine-stricken people of Pingliang and Zhuanglang joined them, and their power revived.

That month Regional Commanders Cao Wenzhao and Yang Jiamou repeatedly defeated rebels at Long'an and Jingning; the rebels fled to Shuiluo Fort, and famine-stricken people of Pingliang and Zhuanglang joined them, and their power revived.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
On maoyin Kong Youde feigned surrender, lured and seized Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Xie Lian, and Laizhou Prefect Zhu Wannian died in the affair.
On guimao Kong Youde feigned surrender, lured and seized Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Xie Lian, and Laizhou Prefect Zhu Wannian died in the affair.
癸卯 is guimao, not maoyin.
Day maoyin: Kong Youde feigned surrender, lured and seized Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Xie Lian, and Laizhou Prefect Zhu Wannian died in the affair.
Day guimao: Kong Youde feigned surrender, lured and seized Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Xie Lian, and Laizhou Prefect Zhu Wannian died in the affair.
癸卯 is guimao, not maoyin.
In spring of Chongzhen six, on maoyin of the first month, Cao Wenbiao was placed in overall command of the generals of Shanxi and Shaanxi to campaign against rebels.
In spring of Chongzhen six, on guimao of the first month, Cao Wenzhao was placed in overall command of the generals of Shanxi and Shaanxi to campaign against rebels.
癸卯 is guimao, not maoyin. 詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
Year six, spring, first month, day maoyin: Cao Wenbiao was placed in overall command of the generals of Shanxi and Shaanxi to campaign against rebels.
Year six, spring, first month, day guimao: Cao Wenzhao was placed in overall command of the generals of Shanxi and Shaanxi to campaign against rebels.
癸卯 is guimao, not maoyin. 詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
That month Cao Wenbiao attacked Shanxi rebels and repeatedly defeated them.
That month Cao Wenzhao attacked Shanxi rebels and repeatedly defeated them.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
That month Cao Wenbiao attacked Shanxi rebels and repeatedly defeated them.
That month Cao Wenzhao attacked Shanxi rebels and repeatedly defeated them.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
In the third month, on guisi, an edict ordered Cao Wenbiao and the generals to suppress the rebels within three months.
In the third month, on guisi, an edict ordered Cao Wenzhao and the generals to suppress the rebels within three months.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
Third month, day guisi: an edict ordered Cao Wenbiao and the generals to suppress the rebels within three months.
Third month, day guisi: an edict ordered Cao Wenzhao and the generals to suppress the rebels within three months.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
In the fifth month, on yisi, the eunuchs Chen Dajin and others were posted in separate assignments to supervise the armies of Cao Wenbiao, Zhang Yingchang, Zuo Liangyu, and Deng Qi.
In the fifth month, on yisi, the eunuchs Chen Dajin and others were posted in separate assignments to supervise the armies of Cao Wenzhao, Zhang Yingchang, Zuo Liangyu, and Deng Qi.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
Fifth month, day yisi: the eunuchs Chen Dajin and others were assigned in separate posts to supervise the armies of Cao Wenbiao, Zhang Yingchang, Zuo Liangyu, and Deng Qi.
Fifth month, day yisi: the eunuchs Chen Dajin and others were assigned in separate posts to supervise the armies of Cao Wenzhao, Zhang Yingchang, Zuo Liangyu, and Deng Qi.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
On guichou Cao Wenbiao was transferred to command at Datong; Shanxi Grand Coordinator Xu Dingchen asked that Wenbiao be kept to suppress rebels, but the request was denied.
On guichou Cao Wenzhao was transferred to command at Datong; Shanxi Grand Coordinator Xu Dingchen asked that Wenzhao be kept to suppress rebels, but the request was denied.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao. The short form 文詔 is Wenzhao, not Wenbiao.
Day guichou: Cao Wenbiao was transferred to command at Datong; Shanxi Grand Coordinator Xu Dingchen requested that Wenbiao be kept to suppress rebels, but permission was not granted.
Day guichou: Cao Wenzhao was transferred to command at Datong; Shanxi Grand Coordinator Xu Dingchen requested that Wenzhao be kept to suppress rebels, but permission was not granted.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao. The short form 文詔 is Wenzhao, not Wenbiao.
In the eighth month, on jisi, Cao Wenbiao defeated rebels at Jiyuan and again defeated them at Huaiqing.
In the eighth month, on jisi, Cao Wenzhao defeated rebels at Jiyuan and again defeated them at Huaiqing.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.
Eighth month, day jisi: Cao Wenbiao defeated rebels at Jiyuan and again defeated them at Huaiqing.
Eighth month, day jisi: Cao Wenzhao defeated rebels at Jiyuan and again defeated them at Huaiqing.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenbiao.

In the eleventh month, on guisi, Vice Ministers of Rites Wang Yingxiong and He Wuyao were both made ministers of rites and grand secretaries of the Eastern Pavilion with a seat in confidential state affairs.

In the eleventh month, on guisi, Vice Ministers of Rites Wang Yingxiong and He Wuzou were both made ministers of rites and grand secretaries of the Eastern Pavilion with a seat in confidential state affairs.
騶 is zou. 何吾騶 is He Wuzou, not He Wuyao.
Eleventh month, day guisi: Vice Ministers of Rites Wang Yingxiong and He Wuyao were both made Ministers of Rites and Grand Secretaries of the Eastern Pavilion, participating in confidential affairs.
Eleventh month, day guisi: Vice Ministers of Rites Wang Yingxiong and He Wuzou were both made Ministers of Rites and Grand Secretaries of the Eastern Pavilion, participating in confidential affairs.
騶 is zou. 何吾騶 is He Wuzou, not He Wuyao.
On jiachen Liu Shun and others received advanced scholar and other degrees in differing ranks.
On jiachen Liu Lishun and others received advanced scholar and other degrees in differing ranks.
理順 is Lishun. 劉理順 is Liu Lishun, not Liu Shun.
Day jiachen: Liu Shun and others were granted advanced scholar and other degrees in differing ranks.
Day jiachen: Liu Lishun and others were granted advanced scholar and other degrees in differing ranks.
理順 is Lishun. 劉理順 is Liu Lishun, not Liu Shun.
On yiwei the court ordered regional commander Chen Hongfan to hold Juyong and Baoding grand coordinator Ding Kuitai and others to hold Zijing and Yanmen.
On yiwei the court ordered regional commander Chen Hongfan to hold Juyong and Baoding grand coordinator Ding Kuichu and others to hold Zijing and Yanmen.
魁楚 is Kuichu. 丁魁楚 is Ding Kuichu, not Ding Kuitai.
Day yiwei: an edict ordered Regional Commander Chen Hongfan to defend Juyong, and Baoding Grand Coordinator Ding Kuitai and others to defend Zijing and Yanmen.
Day yiwei: an edict ordered Regional Commander Chen Hongfan to defend Juyong, and Baoding Grand Coordinator Ding Kuichu and others to defend Zijing and Yanmen.
魁楚 is Kuichu. 丁魁楚 is Ding Kuichu, not Ding Kuitai.
That month Cao Wenchao defeated the bandits at Suizhou.
That month Cao Wenzhao defeated the bandits at Suizhou.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenchao.
That month, Cao Wenchao defeated the bandits at Suizhou.
That month, Cao Wenzhao defeated the bandits at Suizhou.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenchao.
On bingwu Cao Wenchao pursued the bandits to Qiutou Fort in Zhenning, fell into an ambush, and died fighting.
On bingwu Cao Wenzhao pursued the bandits to Qiutou Fort in Zhenning, fell into an ambush, and died fighting.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenchao.
Day bingwu: Cao Wenchao pursued the bandits to Qiutou Fort in Zhenning, fell into an ambush, and died fighting after a fierce struggle.
Day bingwu: Cao Wenzhao pursued the bandits to Qiutou Fort in Zhenning, fell into an ambush, and died fighting after a fierce struggle.
詔 is zhao. 曹文詔 is Cao Wenzhao, not Cao Wenchao.

Winter, tenth month, day gengchen: an edict blamed the emperor himself; he moved his residence to the Wuying Hall, reduced his meals, and withdrew music, showing that he shared hardship with the troops.

Winter, tenth month, day gengchen: he issued an edict of self-reproach; he moved his residence to the Wuying Hall, reduced his meals, and withdrew music, showing that he shared hardship with the troops.
